chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When you pray at the Tree, do not say the Talbiyah until you reach Al-Bayda', where the people say 'The army will be engulfed'.

key_terms.الشَّجَرَةِ: The Tree (Shajarah), a specific location in Mina associated with the Prophet.
key_terms.الْبَيْدَاءَ: Al-Bayda', a plain or open area near Mina.
key_terms.تُلَبِّ: You say the Talbiyah (the ritual invocation of Hajj).
key_terms.يُخْسَفُ بِالْجَيْشِ: The army will be engulfed (a traditional phrase associated with this location).

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim recite the Talbiyah after praying at the Tree in Mina?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise timing for concluding the Talbiyah recitation during Hajj, linking the ritual act to the geographical landmark of Al-Bayda' near the Tree of Abu Juhaynah. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on adhering to specific prophetic traditions regarding the boundaries of sacred rites, ensuring the pilgrim's devotion remains uninterrupted until reaching the designated point of departure for the army's historical engulfment.
